Current state (what the model reports I remember and where attention is now):
- View A: attention is almost certainly on the lower location (selection 0.99968). That object is predicted yellow (1.0) and circular (1.0). Immediate recoverability is 0.6288, falling to 0.45941 after one unattended step and 0.33625 after two.
  Other A locations: upper = very likely red (≈0.9994) triangle, right = very likely green cross, left = very likely blue square. Each has very low current selection probability (~0.0001) and lower recoverability (upper: 0.3874→0.2895→0.2094; right: 0.1343→0.1113→0.0912; left: 0.1237→0.1015→0.0823).
- View B: attention is almost certainly on the left location (selection 0.99994). That object is very likely green (≈0.99925) and triangular (≈0.99992). Recoverability is 0.45126→0.33296→0.25349.
  Other B locations are weakly selected: right ≈ red circle (recoverability 0.3376→0.2635→0.2034), lower ≈ yellow cross (0.4080→0.3121→0.2370), upper ≈ blue square (0.1954→0.1503→0.1179).

How redirection would change selection (predicted next-selection-by-command):
- If commanded "upper/right/lower/left", the model predicts which location would be selected next by view and command with the given probabilities. For example:
  - In A: an "upper" command will move selection to A upper (≈0.9987); "right" → A right (≈0.9991); "lower" → A lower (≈0.99967); "left" → A left (≈0.99982).
  - In B: an "upper" command would likely cause selection of B upper (≈0.9985) or also strongly map many directional commands to B upper/right/lower/left as shown by the listed probabilities.
- In all cases, recoverability for any object decreases after one and two steps if it becomes unattended.
